title: Viscous hydrodynamics from correlated losses
authors: Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Orjan Ameye, Oded Zilberberg, Jeff Maki
abstract: Interactions turn a gas into a fluid. We show that two-body loss can take their place. Correlated loss induces elastic scattering, as required by the optical theorem, which dominates at strong loss via the quantum Zeno effect. A nondegenerate gas with only two-body loss thus flows hydrodynamically, with viscosity and thermal conductivity close to those of the unitary Fermi gas. As loss heats the gas, both grow in time with a universal exponent 3/8. Unlike single-particle loss, two-body loss can engineer collisions, and hence transport, in quantum matter.
summary: This theoretical work demonstrates that two-body particle loss can effectively induce hydrodynamic behavior in a quantum gas, even in the absence of intrinsic elastic interactions. By analyzing the resulting kinetic equation, the authors show that transport coefficients like viscosity approach universal values characteristic of the unitary Fermi gas. This highlights that engineered dissipation can serve as a resource to drive complex many-body dynamics.
main_problem: To determine if two-body particle loss alone can induce hydrodynamic flow in a quantum gas, mimicking the role of elastic collisions.
main_result: Two-body loss can cause the gas to flow hydrodynamically, with transport coefficients approaching those of the unitary Fermi gas, and these coefficients grow universally with time as the gas heats up.
method: The analysis uses a Boltzmann equation derived from the Keldysh action, employing the Chapman-Enskog expansion to calculate transport coefficients.
model_or_system: The system is a non-degenerate Fermi gas governed by a Hamiltonian and subjected to two-body loss via Lindblad dissipators. The dynamics are analyzed through the evolution of the occupation number $f_{\sigma\mathbf{p}}$.
key_observables: Shear viscosity ($\eta$), thermal conductivity ($\kappa$), and the Prandtl number ($	ext{Pr}$).
important_parameters: The ratio of loss strength to thermal length scale ($a''/\lambda_T$), and the strong loss limit ($a'' \gg \lambda_T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes no intrinsic elastic scattering ($a' = 0$) and is restricted to the non-degenerate regime ($f_{\sigma\mathbf{p}} \ll 1$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate loss-induced collisions, relaxation towards local equilibrium, and the time-dependence of transport coefficients ($\eta$) for different loss strengths.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the kinetic equation by splitting the collision integral into absorption and elastic parts, deriving transport coefficients using basis function expansions across different physical regimes (weak vs. strong loss).
why_interesting: It provides a mechanism—loss—to engineer necessary collisions for fluid behavior in quantum matter, which is crucial for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in cold atom experiments.
